tasks.task: Build a timed session plan for one squad

items.when: When you know the sport, ages, numbers, space and kit and need a timed plan with coaching points
Each week in season, to move from last session's notes to this week's plan and messages
When you want a second plan built around one skill and one thing to fix, to compare
When a new skill needs showing first, then practice together, then practice alone
Before the session, to cut overload, spot barriers and add quick checks of who has got it
When the plan has no clear standard for effort and detail that players can control

tasks.task: Make a drill easier and harder for a mixed group

items.when: When a drill is too hard for some, too easy for others, or players are queuing
When one player needs the same drill changed for them without changing what it teaches
When you need the steps from first basics to mastery, to see where a player is stuck
When older and younger players train together and both must gain from one task

tasks.task: Turn a drill into a game players want to play

items.when: When the game must fit the session's theme, space and numbers
When a drill is dull or stressful, to change the challenge, the goal and the feedback
When a few players dominate small groups, to give roles that share the work
When players wait for instructions, to set one shared problem and let the game teach

tasks.task: Break down and teach one technique

items.when: When a technique needs cutting into a few steps, each with a common mistake and a self-check
When you demonstrate, to script what you say aloud so players hear how to decide, not only see
During the session, to ask one quick question that shows who has it and who needs more
When a player has stopped improving and needs one repeatable task with fast feedback

tasks.task: Plan a backup session for bad weather or a small space

items.when: When the pitch is closed, you are in a small hall, or numbers or helpers changed late
When the backup must still follow this week's theme with timings and safety points
When you have ten minutes to re-plan and need a tight minute-by-minute option

tasks.task: Write a season plan with weekly themes and progressions

items.when: When you have the squad, weekly slots and season dates and need a week-by-week plan
Before a season, term or new age group, to go from squad brief to first session in order
When several age groups need a plan where each year builds on the last
Before ordering the weeks, to see which skills must come before which
When the plan teaches each skill once, to bring earlier themes back through the season

tasks.task: Set up a player progress sheet with fair levels

items.when: When you need one sheet per squad with the skills to watch and a simple scale
When "good" for a skill needs clear wording at each level so two coaches agree
When a broad aim such as "better passing" must become things a coach can see
When a full scale is too heavy for a volunteer, to try one standard with room for notes

tasks.task: Write end-of-block notes for players and parents

items.when: At the end of a block or season, to turn the progress sheet into a short note per player
When your draft comments are vague and each player needs one clear thing to work on
Before the notes go out, to check each is specific, useful and fair
When a note labels a child as talented or weak and should name effort and strategy

tasks.task: Write club messages to parents and players

items.when: For start of season, changes, cancellations, kit, consent and end-of-season messages
When a notice is flat, to get a version that puts what parents need first
When families read at mixed levels, to check the message is short and plain enough
When some families read another language and need the same message in it

tasks.task: Handle a complaint or hard talk with a parent

items.when: Before a face-to-face talk, to plan how to listen first and say your side once
When an angry message arrives and you need a calm reply that promises only what you can do
When your own draft is sharp, to get a version the parent will want to help with
Before you send a reply, to check promises, facts and tone
When two families or a parent and a coach are in dispute and need ground rules

tasks.task: Give a player feedback that changes behaviour

items.when: When you must raise effort, attitude or behaviour with one player and want the words
When a player means well but does not follow through, to agree simple if-then plans
When you are about to label a child and should describe what you saw and set a limit
When a player gives up after a setback and needs a next strategy, not a verdict

tasks.task: Set goals with a player and keep them motivated

items.when: When a player's aim is fuzzy and needs a number and a finish line
When the squad should set and review their own goals each block
When players resist one part of training, to rebuild it around choice and progress
When goals are about results and should be about what to practise this week

tasks.task: Write a volunteer coach handbook

items.when: When the club has policies and contacts and coaches need one short guide to follow
When volunteer roles, screening and training are not yet agreed by the club
When each role, such as coach, helper and team manager, needs a one-page job card
When a club policy is written in formal words and coaches need it in plain ones
Before it is printed, to check a busy volunteer can read it in one sitting

tasks.task: Induct and support new volunteer coaches

items.when: When a new coach starts and needs an induction, a practice plan and named supervision
When inductions are done, to see whose checks or supervised sessions are still missing
When a new volunteer takes over a squad and needs the first weeks laid out
When you watch a new coach's session and need look-fors and a sheet to record facts
After watching a session, to plan a short talk that ends in one small next step

tasks.task: Write head-injury steps for parents and coaches

items.when: At the start of a season, or when the club adopts a concussion policy
When the governing body's policy is long and coaches need what changes for them
Before it goes out, to check every time limit and rule against the source you were given

tasks.task: Write a factual welfare concern note

items.when: When you saw or heard something worrying and must pass it to the welfare officer today
To confirm who the welfare officer is and the route the club says to use

tasks.task: Adapt a session for players with access needs

items.when: When a player has a disability or support need and the session must work for them too
When a plan is drafted, to find what will shut some players out and what design can fix
When one drill needs changing for one player with the aim kept the same
When the same change can help by giving every drill an easier and a harder level

tasks.task: Plan basic fitness work for an adult beginner group

items.when: When adult beginners want a simple four-week plan with warm-ups and rest days
When fitness work must sit inside a normal session with timings and safety points

tasks.task: Prepare match day: team talk and match messages

items.when: When you have notes for a team talk and need it short and shaped to be heard
When parents need the time, place, kit and lift details for a match or event
When the talk is about winning and should be about effort and what players control

tasks.task: Plan a tournament, trial or open day

items.when: When visitors with access needs will come and you need routes and who does what
When the event needs a poster with checked details and an export list
When there are no good photos, to try a type-only poster that reads from far away
When families need the event details, what to bring and how to sign up

tasks.task: Write posts to recruit players and volunteers

items.when: When the club needs clear posts for a new season, a trial or a call for helpers
When the call for volunteers is flat, to lead with what the helper gains
When a volunteer will make the graphic from a template and reuse it
When a volunteer or sponsor should be thanked with one specific, true line
Before the posts go up, so a fresh reader checks they say who, where, when and how to join
Before posting, to confirm the sign-up link works and the trial dates and places are still open

tasks.task: Ask for a grant, a sponsor or set fees

items.when: When the club needs kit or pitch money and does not know which funders fit
When a funder's form is open and you need a draft matched to their questions
When a local business might sponsor the kit and you need tiers and pitch words
When the club must set or change fees and wants fair tiers
Before the bid or sponsor pack is sent, so a fresh reader in the funder's seat lists what they would ask

tasks.task: Read parent and player feedback at season end

items.when: Before you act on a survey, to find the answers that cannot be trusted
When you have survey answers and messages and need themes ranked with quotes

always.when: Before any message or handout goes out, to catch typos and names spelt two ways
When a document states a safety rule, ratio or time limit you cannot trace to the source

helpers.when: When the job is recruiting, rostering and keeping volunteers, not coaching them
When posters, kit graphics or social templates must look finished
When the club wants a posting plan for the season, not one post
When a grant bid or fundraising drive is the main job
When a tournament or camp needs a full run sheet, suppliers and a budget
When the club is selling sponsor packages to several businesses

gaps: The library has no sport-specific items; session plans, drills and season plans rest on the kit and on classroom teaching skills
No library item holds drills or small-sided games by sport, age and skill
No library item plans age-appropriate warm-ups, conditioning or training load for children
No library item covers match day: fair playing time, selection, substitutions or a half-time talk
No library item covers safeguarding: welfare concern notes, supervision ratios or photo consent
No library item covers concussion or injury steps, a session risk assessment or an emergency action plan
No library item builds a player progress tracker or an attendance register
No library item gives clearly different versions of one club message to compare, or checks a club message for missing details
No library item plans tournament fixtures, a holiday camp or a volunteer rota
No library item writes a short parent or player survey
No library item covers video review of a player's technique
No library item checks a recruitment post, a grant bid or a sponsor pitch for a club before it goes out
